questions.text:
C onsider the following parse tree for the expression a#b$c$d#e#f, involving two binary operators $ and #.

Which one of the following is correct for the given parse tree?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- $ appears deeper in the tree than #, so it is applied first [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] $ has higher precedence.
- b $ c $ d is grouped as (b $ c) $ d [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] $ is left associative.
- a # ([latex]\ldots[/latex] # (e # f)) groups to the right [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] # is right associative.

Answer: $ has higher precedence and is left associative; # is right associative

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: [latex]\$[/latex] has higher precedence and is left associative; # is right associative
# has higher precedence and is left associative; [latex]\$[/latex] is right associative
[latex]\$[/latex] has higher precedence and is left associative; # is left associative
# has higher precedence and is right associative; [latex]\$[/latex] is left associative

questions.text:
A lexical analyzer uses the following patterns to recognize three tokens [latex]T_{1}, T_{2}, \; and \; T_{3} [/latex] over the alphabet {a,b,c}.

[latex]T_{1}:a?(b|c)^* a [/latex]
[latex]T_{2}:b?(a|c)^* b [/latex]
[latex] T_{3}:c?(b|a)^* c[/latex]

Note that 'x?' means 0 or 1 occurrence of the symbol x. Note also that the analyzer outputs the token that matches the longest possible prefix.

If the string bbaacabc is processed by the analyzer, which one of the following is the sequence of tokens it outputs?
questions.solution:
Longest-prefix matching on bbaacabc:
- T1 matches "bba", T2 matches "bb", but T3 = c?(b|a)*c matches "bbaac" (longest) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T3
- Remaining "abc": T3 matches "abc" [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T3

Answer: T3T3

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: [latex]T_{1}T_{2}T_{3}[/latex]
[latex]T_{1}T_{1}T_{3}[/latex]
[latex]T_{2}T_{1}T_{3}[/latex]
[latex]T_{3}T_{3}[/latex]

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is FALSE?
questions.solution:
Type checking is part of semantic analysis, which comes after parsing (it needs the syntax tree). So "type checking is done before parsing" is false. The other statements are true.

Answer: Type checking is done before parsing
